(expectations investing / reverse DCF), and (c) choose a systematic method you can stick with through a bad 1–3 years. Behavioral staying power is itself the edge.

`person:prashant-jain` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, process, contrarian, value, sector-psu

Managed HDFC Equity (from Zurich India days, ~1994) and HDFC Top 100 until July 2022 (~28 years). HDFC Equity: ~19.3% CAGR since launch and beat its benchmark in 18 of 21 years; ~20% 20-year CAGR vs ~9.7% for the Nifty (Outlook). Process: valuation discipline, low turnover, willingness to look wrong for years; avoided the 2000 tech bubble and the 2007 realty mania at peak multiples, and leaned into unloved large caps (PSU banks, power, oil, capital goods). His line: 'If there is no pain, why should valuations be attractive?' Structural edge: very large AUM in an era when Indian MF competition was thin; later, size became a constraint (Business Standard 2013). Biggest mistake: 2018-2020 underperformance from an outsized bet on PSUs (SBI, NTPC, Coal India, BPCL etc.) whose value did not turn into growth, causing heavy redemptions and Morningstar downgrades; the PSU bets finally paid off in the last ~18 months of his HDFC stint. Founded 3P Investment Managers (May 2023), >Rs 15,000 crore AUM in two funds. Copyable: valuation discipline in large caps and the stamina to hold an underweight in bubbles; but recognise that cheap PSUs can stay cheap for years without a catalyst (capex cycle, NPA clean-up).

`strategy:thorp-kelly` | confidence: **verified** | tags: global, process, quant, position-sizing, avoid-ruin

Kelly criterion: for a bet with win probability p and payoff odds b, the growth-maximising fraction of capital is f = (bp - q)/b, where q = 1 - p. Thorp's practice: (1) bet only where expectation is demonstrably positive (counted cards, mispriced warrants/convertibles); (2) size at a fraction of Kelly (half or less) because inputs are uncertain and full Kelly produces brutal drawdowns - roughly a 50% chance of halving the bankroll at some point; (3) hedge out risks you are not paid for (market-neutral). Translation for a stock investor: edge estimates are noisy, so practical position caps (e.g., 5-10% at cost for high conviction, 1-3% for speculative) approximate fractional Kelly; never use leverage or F&O sizes that can wipe you out (see SEBI's F&O loss studies). Feasibility test (Thorp's Madoff insight): if a track record is too smooth for the claimed strategy, verify it or walk away. Evidence quality: Kelly is mathematically proven for repeated bets with known odds; real markets violate those assumptions, which is why fractional Kelly is the rule.

| Revenue per store per yr | ₹17.3 cr | ~₹134 cr [EST: ₹66,968 cr ÷ avg(415, 500) stores] | — | [EST] |
| Gross margin | 28.4% [AR26] | ~15% [SCR: material cost 85%] | ~30% [SCR: material 70%] | |
| **Gross profit per sq ft per yr** | **~₹2,860** | **~₹5,000** | ~₹3,300 | [EST] = rev/sq ft × GM |

**Lesson:** VMM's 28% gross margin looks twice DMart's 15%. But DMart turns each square foot about 3.3× faster, so it earns about 75% *more* gross profit per square foot. Margin % without density is half a number. (DMart also owns most of its stores, so its occupancy cost is capex rather than rent. That is the next layer.)

- **V2 Retail is the cannibalisation and immaturity warning for the format.** V2 sold ₹700 per sq ft per month in Q2 FY27 against ₹933 a year earlier, after 139 stores were added in FY26 and SSSG went negative (−3.7% H1, calendar basis). Source: V2 Q2 FY27 transcript summary, single-source. Fast rollout in the same value format can dilute density sharply. VMM's 5.4% Q2 SSSG (about 9% festive-adjusted) has not shown this, but it is the metric to watch.

body:
1. **The deepest data was free and audited.** BRSR (minimum-wage share, attrition, headcount, median pay) plus annual-report note 24 (security, manpower, housekeeping) plus note 35 (related parties) beat every broker report on cost drivers. Most investors never open the BRSR.
2. **"Security-guard depth" is a ratio, not a curiosity.** Guard cost per store ÷ state minimum wage → guards per store → a ground-checkable number. The same chain links wages to margin sensitivity.
3. **Every company-defined metric (SSSG, payback, loyalty customers, "operating EBITDA") needs its footnote read.** Three of the four had a definitional catch.
4. **Peers expose what the company won't.** DMart's density shows what VMM's margin hides. V2 Retail's density collapse shows the rollout risk VMM has not yet shown.
5. Time spent: about 70% on primary documents, 20% on estimates, 10% on broker notes. Broker notes were most useful as a **map of what management said in closed analyst meets** (category GM premiums, DC capacity, RFID cost).

body:
**Question.** `insight:disqualifiers` (revised 20-Nov-2026, L10/L12) splits our checklist into HARD
disqualifiers (no override) and GRADED flags (override with `insight:flag-override-template`). Do the hard
rules catch traps (fraud, blow-ups, >70% losses) *at the time we would have been deciding*, and how many
winners would they and the graded flags have cost us?

**Part A — labelled case set.** Every `case_study` in memdb (131 records). Duplicates (hidden-trap-X / X,
false-alarm-X / X) merged into one company-episode; 14 non-company or private records excluded with a
reason. Labels: WINNER (≥3x from T), TRAP (fraud / blow-up / >70% loss from T not recovered within 5 years,
sub-typed fraud, lev = leverage/business blow-up, bust = valuation/cycle round-trip after a run), FALSE-ALARM
(the flags-judgment library; counted as winners). T = episode start: for traps the peak / last calm date
before the first public shock; for winners the record's start (trough, IPO or start of the measured leg).
**Hindsight rule:** a flag counts as fired only if the record or a dated filing shows it was public before T.
If that cannot be shown, it is `U` (unknown), never `Y`. Flags that became public after T are kept as
"later" notes (early-warning value), not hits. Mechanical flags use only fiscal years public before T
(India: FY ending March counts from 30 Sep; US: period end + 90 days) from screener.in pages (India) and SEC
companyfacts (US); promoter pledge from the BSE shareholding-pattern XBRL filed before T.

Rules tested (codes used everywhere below):
- HARD: H1a fake-cash signal · H1b economics implausible for the business · H1c profits not verifiable by
  outsiders · H2 auditor resignation citing disagreement/denied information or qualified opinion ·
  H3 rating "issuer not cooperating" · H4 SME/Telegram pump · H5 related-party cash leakage to promoter
  entities. Plus a broader variant **H2b**: any auditor exit mid-term, restatement / SEC 8-K item 4.02,
  regulator-assessed misstatement (e.g., RBI NPA divergence) or delayed results within 5 years before T.
- GRADED: G1 promoter pledge > 25% of promoter holding · G3 dilution / repeated raises in the 2 years
  before T · G4 trailing P/E > 50 (or > 2x own median) · and mechanical: F1 Σ5y CFO/Σ5y PAT < 0.7,
  F1b < 0.3, G2 borrowings ≥ 1.5x over 3 years with Σ3y CFO < 0, G5 Σ5y FCF < 0, G6 debtor days > 120 or
  +30 days in 2 years, F2 other income > 30% of PBT (3y). Lenders: cash-flow, debtor-day and other-income
  tests marked not applicable.

body:
**Layers for a lender.**
- **L2:** re-derive PPOP = NII + other income − opex; split other income into fees / treasury / one-offs; rebuild the
  **NPA walk** (opening + slippage − recoveries − **write-offs** = closing); compute ratios on **average** balances;
  separate company "excl one-off" figures and keep both. Read the integrated-filing XBRL (`nse_fetch.py integrated`;
  Q1/Q3 filings carry no balance sheet for banks).
- **L3 unit economics:** per outlet — deposits, CASA, advances, revenue, opex, staff, rent, PAT; liability value of a
  mature branch (CASA × saving vs wholesale rate) vs its direct cost; new-branch break-even CASA; per employee —
  loaded cost vs BRSR median, attrition.
- **L4 cost lines in physical terms:** staff (headcount × **IBA bipartite scale**; settlement dates are dated,
  public, leading); **DICGC premium** (≈ 12 paise per ₹100 of assessable deposits; cross-foot insurance ÷ 0.0012 ≈
  deposits); outsourcing/service charges and card-network charges (scale with volumes); rent per outlet.
  Balance-sheet cost lines that sit in NIM: **CRR** (NDTL × CRR% × opportunity rate), **PSL-shortfall deposits**
  (RIDF/NABARD/SIDBI balance × (loan yield − RIDF rate)), SLR carry.
- **L4 rate and funding mechanics:** EBLR/MCLR/fixed split × repo move = immediate yield change; deposit repricing lag
  (~1 year for TDs); special windows (FCNR, TLTRO-type) that inflate both sides of the balance sheet — always
  re-derive growth **ex** the window (loans against the new deposits).
- **L4 asset quality:** slippage and GNPA by segment ÷ segment book; collateral price sensitivity (gold LTV, property);
  vintage/cohort data if disclosed (rarely; say so); ECL/regulatory transitions dated with the guided impact.
- **L5:** no promoter often — the related parties are management (pay mix, ESOP, variable-pay caps), the strategic
  investor (warrants, board seat), subsidiaries (connected lending); the **CEO's RBI-approved term end** is a dated
  watch item.
- **L6 scuttlebutt:** branch counts and rate boards; a fixed gold-loan price basket vs PSU banks and NBFCs; gold
  auction notices (public, dated); NRI exchange houses; RBI BSR (state deposits/credit), RBI card statistics, NPCI
  bank performance, RBI Ombudsman complaints; fintech-partner apps and directions; union notices on wage talks.
- **L7:** bad-but-benign vs good-but-misleading table is mandatory (at Federal Bank: 10 misleading-good vs 6 benign-bad).

**Valuation (L8) for lenders:** `worksheet.py` with `"mode": "bank"` (`tools/valuation/bank.py`): P/B fully diluted for
warrants/QIPs; ROE needed forever `g + P/B × (CoE − g)`; **implied CoE at today's ROE** `g + (ROE − g) ÷ P/B`;
residual-income scenarios on an ROE path with an exit P/B and its RIM-consistent P/B; book stress (+1/2/3/5% loan
loss as % of book); own 10-yr P/B band and peer P/Bs. Expect the same CoE dominance as L21: read the implied CoE,
the base-case IRR and the P/B band.
